title: Frame.io vs Gigxomi for Video Editing Agencies
excerpt: Compare Frame.io's specialist video review and asset collaboration with Gigxomi's broader agency operating workflow from enquiry to payout.
seoDescription: Frame.io vs Gigxomi for video editing agencies: compare specialist video review and asset collaboration with end-to-end agency operations.
featuredImageAlt: Frame.io versus Gigxomi video agency comparison
introduction: Frame.io and Gigxomi solve different layers of video operations. Frame.io specializes in media collaboration: assets, versions, frame-accurate feedback, shares, and production-to-post workflows. Gigxomi focuses on running the editing business around that media: client enquiries, managers, editors, tasks, review, delivery, accounting, and payouts. For many serious teams, this is a stack decision rather than a replacement contest.
verdict: Choose Frame.io when precise audiovisual review, version control, secure sharing, storage, and integrations with creative production are the decisive requirements. Choose Gigxomi when the agency's larger problem is moving commercial work and people from enquiry through delivery and payout. An agency can reasonably use Frame.io as the review room and Gigxomi as the operating layer, provided ownership and status synchronization are clear.

sections.heading: Where Frame.io remains the specialist
paragraphs: Video feedback is spatial and temporal. A reviewer may need to identify a frame, draw on the image, compare versions, or discuss a precise range. Generic task comments rarely provide the same clarity. Frame.io is designed around the media object and the reviewer's experience, which can reduce ambiguous notes and version confusion.

Its asset and production capabilities also matter for teams handling large files and professional creative workflows. Secure presentation, transfers, storage, and camera-origin workflows are not minor add-ons. An agency should not abandon that depth merely because another platform includes a review status.
bullets: Integrations close to professional creative workflows

sections.heading: What Frame.io does not try to be
paragraphs: A review workspace typically begins after a client relationship and production assignment already exist. It does not need to be the place where an Instagram enquiry is qualified, a manager routes the opportunity, an editor's commercial terms are tracked, or payout visibility is maintained. Forcing those concerns into folders and comments weakens a strong specialist tool.

Gigxomi addresses that surrounding business. The useful architecture may therefore be Gigxomi for client and work ownership, with Frame.io links attached at the review stage. The main design question is which system declares approval final and triggers delivery.

sections.heading: Design a clean two-tool workflow
paragraphs: Create the project and accountable owners in Gigxomi, then create or link the correct Frame.io review destination when a cut is ready. Put creative comments in Frame.io, not in parallel chat threads. When the designated reviewer marks the correct version approved, update the project milestone in Gigxomi and preserve the approved share or asset reference.

Define naming rules before volume grows. Client code, project code, deliverable name, aspect ratio, and version should match across both products. Managers should never guess whether 'final-v7-new' is newer than 'final-approved'. The system boundary works only when identity and approval semantics are unambiguous.

sections.heading: Migration advice from a Frame.io-only setup
paragraphs: Do not migrate master media into an operations platform simply for consolidation. Keep assets and review history where their integrity and sharing controls are strongest. Instead, inventory active projects, customers, responsible managers, editors, deadlines, current approved version links, and commercial state for import into Gigxomi.

Introduce the operating layer on new work first. Add existing projects only when they still require meaningful coordination or payment action. Train the team that Frame.io answers 'what changed in the video?' while Gigxomi answers 'who owns the job, where is it in the business, and what happens next?'

sections.heading: When one product may be enough
paragraphs: Frame.io alone may be enough for an internal post-production team whose projects and finance are already managed reliably elsewhere and whose main pain is review. Gigxomi alone may be enough for a smaller editing agency with straightforward review requirements and a greater need for connected client and team operations.

Use both when losing frame-level clarity would harm creative quality and losing business-level traceability would harm delivery or cash flow. The extra subscription and integration discipline are justified only if each product has a distinct owner and measurable role.

decisionChecklist: Do reviewers need frame-level annotations and version comparison?
Where should master media and approval history live?
Which system declares the final approved version?
How will project and deliverable names match across tools?
Are client acquisition and editor payout currently disconnected from review?
Can one product meet current volume without weakening controls?
